english.title: Seize / exercise control of a maritime fixed platform by use of threats or force
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) unlawfully, by the use of force or threats,

(A)_[seized]_
(B)_[exercised control of]_

a fixed platform, namely **(..SPECIFY FIXED PLATFORM..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 10(1) and (2) of the Aviation and Maritime Security Act 1990.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
unlawfully by use of force/threats
seized/exercised control of a fixed platform

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) It does not matter the nationality the accused claims or whether the ship is in the United Kingdom (section 10(1)).
(ii) The consent of the Attorney General is required.
(iii) See section 17 for definitions.
(iv) Terrorist connection - this offence is listed in Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 2020. Where the court has determined that there is a terrorist connection, the court has to treat this as an aggravating factor in sentencing (section 69 of that Act) and the notification requirements under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 apply (section 42 of that Act). In addition, section 23A of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides for forfeiture of money or other property.

other.penalty:
Life imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
